back: A rotating low-pressure storm that forms over warm tropical oceans with sustained winds of at least 119 km/h; hurricane (Atlantic), typhoon (north-west Pacific), cyclone (Indian Ocean and Australia).
Sea at least about 26.5 °C to 50 m depth; latitude about 5° to 30° (Coriolis effect); low wind shear; moist air and a disturbance; late summer or autumn.
Category 1: 119–153 km/h; 2: 154–177; 3: 178–208; 4: 209–251; 5: 252 km/h or more. It measures wind only.
A rise in sea level above the normal tide caused by winds and low pressure; the main cause of deaths on low-lying coasts.
They lose the supply of warm moist air and heat, and friction slows the winds; heavy rain can continue and cause floods and landslides.
Landfall near Beira, Mozambique; flooding in the Buzi and Pungwe plains and landslides in Chimanimani, Zimbabwe; more than a thousand deaths in three countries (rounded).
Shelters, a trained volunteer programme, embankments and warnings: deaths fell from about 300 000 in 1970 to about 3 400 in Cyclone Sidr (2007).
Expected: heavier rainfall (about 7% per °C), higher surge as sea level rises, and a larger share of the strongest storms; no clear increase in the total number.
Forecasts and warnings, shelters and evacuation, defences (embankments and mangroves), building design and land use, education and drills, recovery plans.
